text.p: VIENNA July 9 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Wednesday are:
DER STANDARD

- Conservative People's Party of Wolfgang Schuessel loses two percentage points over the last three weeks to score a rating of 22 percent. His alleged insult of Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer is partly to blame. The People's Party now lies significantly behind the Social Democrats at 36 percent and the far-right Freedom Party at 28 percent.
- Cabinet meeting decides to release the first billion schillings put aside for technology this year.
- Foreign Minister Schuessel defends himself before a special parliament question time, insisting he never insulted Tietmeyer and others.
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger assures "there will not be a third savings packet" but does concede that the budgets for the next years will need some "measures in part on the income side."
DIE PRESSE
- Opposition parties announce their intent of bringing three votes of no confidence against Schuessel on Friday.
- Austria suffers worst rainfall this century with whole areas cut off by flooding.
- A three-day conference of 11 leaders of Eastern Europe begins today in Salzburg to discuss "Europe's growing market" and the enlargement of NATO and the EU.
- A women's conference "Vital Voices" begins in Vienna today, and will be attended by thousands of women from around the world including U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton.
- The Austrian government issued its first-ever 30-year bond with a coupon of 6.25 percent.
- Austria's exporters are benefiting from the strong dollar.
- VAI, a subsidiary of VA Tech, received an order worth some one billion schillings to build a complete steelworks in Egypt.
- Dairy products group NOeM found itself again mired deep in red figures last year. Pretax profit improved just 2.2 million schillings to a loss of 215.2 million schillings.
- Creditanstalt's director of the board Gerhard Novy says fears of a weak euro are groundless and sees EMU kicking off with 11 members.
- The Austrian branch of Deutsche Bank sees great opportunities in the area of personal investment.
KURIER
- Heavy rainfall has caused damage in the billions of schillings.
- Motorbike maker KTM turns in a 20 percent increase in sales in the first nine months of its 1996/97 businees year.
- Both coalition partners agree that the government's stake in market leader Bank Austria must be sold by the end of March next year.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- KTM plans to buy an 80 percent stake of WP Suspension of the Netherlands.
